root.label: Contracts (C++26)
root.note: Redundant checks via pre, post and contract_assert; how they are checked is chosen by the implementation.

children.label: Three assertion kinds
children.note: Preconditions, postconditions and assertion statements, each with a bool predicate.

children.label: pre(expr)
children.note: Checked after parameters are initialized, before the body runs, in lexical order.

children.label: post(r: expr)
children.note: Checked on normal return only; r is a const lvalue naming the result object.

children.label: contract_assert(expr);
children.note: A full keyword and a statement; unaffected by NDEBUG, unlike the assert macro.

children.label: Placement rules
children.note: Specifiers attach to the function's first declaration and are not part of its type.

children.label: First declaration
children.note: Later declarations omit them or repeat the same sequence; adding or partly repeating is an error.

children.label: Not in the type
children.note: Ignored by overload resolution; pointers to functions and type aliases cannot carry them.

children.label: Banned in C++26
children.note: Virtual functions, deleted functions, and functions defaulted on first declaration. Virtual support is C++29 (P3097).

children.label: Lambdas and coroutines
children.note: Allowed. Contract-only uses cannot trigger implicit capture; coroutine posts cannot read by-value parameters.

children.label: Const predicates
children.note: Outside variables, *this and the result binding are const inside a predicate.

children.label: Implicit const
children.note: Calling a non-const member or incrementing a parameter in a predicate is ill-formed.

children.label: Const parameters for post
children.note: A by-value parameter read in a postcondition must be const on every declaration.

children.label: Side effects
children.note: Still possible via mutable or const_cast; a predicate may run zero, one or several times.

children.label: Evaluation semantics
children.note: Implementation-defined per evaluation; enforce is the recommended default.

children.label: ignore
children.note: Predicate not evaluated, but still odr-used, so it must compile.

children.label: observe
children.note: Checked; on violation the handler runs and execution continues if it returns.

children.label: enforce
children.note: Checked; handler runs, then the program is contract-terminated if it returns.

children.label: quick-enforce
children.note: Checked; contract-terminated at once without calling the handler.

children.label: Constant evaluation
children.note: A violation is ill-formed under a terminating semantic and a diagnostic under observe.

children.label: Violation handling
children.note: ::handle_contract_violation receives a const std::contracts::contract_violation&.

children.label: Replaceable handler
children.note: Replaceability is implementation-defined; __cpp_lib_replaceable_contract_violation_handler reports it.

children.label: Observers
children.note: kind, semantic, is_terminating, detection_mode, comment, location. GCC 16 spells detection_mode as mode.

children.label: Throwing predicate
children.note: A violation; the handler runs inside an active handler for that exception.

children.label: Throwing handler
children.note: Acts as if the function body threw; in a noexcept function, std::terminate is called.

children.label: Related features
children.note: How contracts differ from older and neighbouring mechanisms.

children.label: [[assume]]
children.note: A false assumption is UB; contracts never let the optimizer assume an unchecked predicate.

children.label: C++20 attributes
children.note: [[expects]], [[ensures]] and [[assert]] with levels were removed in 2019 before shipping.

children.label: Library hardening
children.note: In a hardened implementation, library Hardened preconditions are checked with a terminating semantic.
